data.title: ZAWYA: Air Arabia-led consortium gets green light for new Saudi budget carrier in Dammam
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) has granted a consortium led by Air Arabia an Air Operator Certificate (AOC) to launch the Kingdom’s new national low-cost carrier, based at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

The certificate was issued in the presence of Minister of Transport and Logistic Services and GACA Chairman Saleh Al-Jasser, and GACA President Abdulaziz Al-Duailej, following the consortium’s successful completion of regulatory and operational requirements covering safety, security and operational quality.

The consortium, comprising Air Arabia Group, Nesma Group and KUN Holding Company, was selected by GACA in July 2025 as the winning bidder to establish and operate the new airline, with majority Saudi ownership.

The carrier is expected to create more than 2,400 direct jobs, contribute to GDP growth and strengthen tourism and air connectivity in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province, supporting the objectives of the Kingdom’s aviation programme.

Sulaiman Almuhaimedi, Executive Vice President of Aviation Safety and Environmental Sustainability at GACA, said that granting the AOC to the new carrier represents a significant step towards the Kingdom’s aviation strategy which aims to position Saudi Arabia as a global logistics hub and an international aviation hub.

He added: “The launch of Air Arabia’s operations from Dammam will contribute to enhancing competition and improving performance in the air transport market, while supporting trade and tourism in the Eastern Province and creating new local employment opportunities.”

He noted that the license was granted after the airline successfully completed all the required technical and regulatory stages and procedures to ensure the highest levels of safety and operational compliance. He further highlighted that this milestone reflects GACA’s role as the regulator of the air transport industry and its efforts to create an attractive investment environment.

He also noted that the new carrier will strengthen the Kingdom’s air connectivity by serving 24 domestic and 57 international destinations and is expected to carry approximately 10 million passengers annually by 2030, in line with the goals of the aviation programme.

data.title: HC Orders Review of 1, Other Extremely Low Defence Bids
data.description:
Manu Pubby New Delhi: In a ruling that can have far-reaching consequences for the defence industry, the Andhra Pradesh High Court has held that contracts cannot be mechanically awarded to the lowest bidder when the quoted price is so low that it raises doubts about the company's ability to deliver. Last week, the Andhra Pradesh High Court at Amaravati said that when a bid value is abnormally low, a viability assessment needs to be conducted before the contract is awarded.

The court ruling came in a case concerning the development-cum-production partnership (DCPP) model of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), under which companies are invited to co-develop weapon technologies. Firms are initially invited to bid for a limited development order, typically covering a small number of prototypes.

The lowest-ranked bidders selected under the tender then work with DRDO to develop, test and demonstrate the system against the stipulated performance requirements. Once the equipment clears the required developmental and user trials and is found fit for operational induction, the armed forces can place larger production orders. Because the initial development phase is limited in quantity but carries high upfront costs, including engineering, trials and certification, companies may be willing to absorb part of the initial expenditure, or even incur losses, at that stage in the expectation of a larger follow-on order.

There have been instances in the past where abnormally low bids have been placed during DCPP competitions. In one particular case, a company even submitted a bid of one rupee to develop prototypes, resulting in it being selected as the DCPP winner for a weapon urgently needed by the armed forces. The Andhra HC ruling came in a petition filed by defence player Jaykay Enterprises regarding a DCPP project to develop the processor-based moored mine - next generation.

The company alleged that the winner of the contract, Apollo Micro Systems, had submitted an abnormally low bid that did not even cover the basic cost of materials required to manufacture the mines. In its judgement, the HC referred to a procedural failure on the part of DRDO, as it had not conducted a pre-award scrutiny for an abnormally low bid, as mandated under the DRDO Procurement Manual, 2025. It has asked the relevant authorities to conduct the scrutiny and proceed with the contract only if all conditions are met.

data.title: Code of Conduct Only for Smaller Cos?
data.description:
Tanya Pandey A call by Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei to slow the pace of frontier artificial intelligence (AI) development has opened up a much wider debate over how fast the technology should advance. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, xAI chief Elon Musk, Microsoft chief Satya Nadella and even the United Nations human rights chief Volker Turk have since joined Dario to call for a pause, as concerns over AI safety meet questions around the cost of building frontier models, the loss of jobs, impact on the environment along with its use for autonomous and dangerous weapons.

But are the calls for pacing development genuinely about bringing in greater oversight or is a ploy for a cover up, Tanya Pandey explains. What are the calls for a slowdown, what do they comprise? The calls are not for stopping AI development. They are about giving safety testing and oversight more time to keep up with increasingly capable models, through independent evaluations, common safety standards, and greater coordination between companies and governments.

Why is it an issue now? AI systems are becoming more autonomous and are taking on tasks that previously required humans. They are also increasingly being used to write code and help develop other AI systems, raising concerns that capabilities could improve faster than companies can understand and control them. Former employees of some of these labs have come out in the open to express concerns and have even warned that AI could kill humans by end of this decade.

Could the slowdown also protect big AI labs? As Chinese open-weight models such as Kimi K3, DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Z.ai's GLM become increasingly capable at a fraction of the cost of leading US models, tighter government controls could make it harder for smaller companies and open source developers to compete with the biggest labs.

Some critics argue this could help the leading AI companies retain their advantage. How is the market reacting to the calls? The AI boom has created a huge investment chain around chips, data centres and computing infrastructure. Investors are now assessing what a slower pace of frontier AI development could mean for that spending. SoftBank fell as much as 13.2%, while Kioxia, SK Hynix, Samsung, TSMC and Tokyo Electron also declined.

Is the AI industry also facing an economic problem? The cost of training frontier models has risen massively. Training some of the largest models now costs hundreds of millions of dollars, with future frontier training runs expected to cross $1 billion. At the same time, open source models are becoming more capable and cheaper, raising questions over whether frontier labs can keep spending at this pace.

How does the AI slowdown tie into the US-China race? The argument is that the US should maintain its lead while putting safeguards around frontier development, alongside tighter controls on advanced AI technology going to China. Beijing has rejected that approach, with its Foreign Ministry saying that "fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition" would disrupt global AI governance.

What do IPO plans tell us about AI industry's position? The slowdown debate comes as biggest AI labs face massive commercial expectations. OpenAI has pushed its IPO plans out of 2026, after reportedly eyeing a valuation of around $1 trillion. Anthropic is preparing for a potential IPO and is reportedly seeking a valuation of over $2 trillion.

data.title: Solar Acquires South African Explosives Co Omnia for $1.3b
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Nagpur-headquartered Solar Industries has acquired South Africa's Omnia Holdings for $1.3 billion in one of the largest outbound mergers and acquisitions deals in the defence sector.

Solar's wholly owned, step-down subsidiary Solar SA Investments Pty will acquire all outstanding shares of Johannesburg Stock Exchange-listed Omnia in an all-cash transaction, the company said in a stock exchange disclosure on Monday. The deal is expected to enable Solar Industries to establish a platform for commercial explosives and blasting solutions internationally. "The acquisition by Solar SA of Omnia will create an integrated global blasting platform that combines Omnia's vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities, ammonium nitrate production, surface bulk explosives and blasting services with Solar Group's leadership in explosives, initiating systems and advanced blasting technologies," said Manish Nuwal, managing director and chief executive officer, Solar Group.

Solar Industries will also be buying Omnia's integrated crop nutrition and biological solutions business. The Nagpur-headquartered company currently makes explosives for defence and industrial applications. Its explosives are used as propellants for missiles as well as in the mining industry. Solar has also diversified its manufacturing activities to include supplies of loitering munitions and counter-drone systems. "Together, the combined group will be positioned to offer integrated blasting solutions, creating meaningful competitive advantages through enhanced supply security, greater economies of scale, technology differentiation, access to key mining markets across Africa and other international geographies, and deeper customer engagement," Nuwal said.

Solar reported FY26 revenue of Rs 9,965 crore ($1.03 billion) and has an order book of Rs 11,000 crore ($1.1 billion) from the defence sector as per its website. Omnia is a diversified global group with complementary chemical and specialised businesses serving customers across the mining, agriculture and chemicals sectors.

It has a physical presence in 23 countries and serves customers in more than 40 through 70 distribution centres, employing 3,500 people worldwide. It posted FY26 revenue of $1.4 billion. Manufacturers of explosives for defence applications have been looking to expand business in the backdrop of increased spending and the government's focus on indigenisation. Apollo Micro Systems recently acquired explosives manufacturer Premier Explosives for Rs 2,500 crore, enabling it to expand trinitrotoluene (TNT) capacity.

data.title: SB Energy Could Raise Up to $500 Million in Japan as Part of U.S. Listing
data.description:
By Kosaku Narioka

SB Energy could raise up to $500 million in Japan as part of its planned listing in the U.S.

The SoftBank Group unit said Tuesday that the amount to be raised in Japan would be decided at a later date when the offering price is determined, expected between September 2026 and February 2027.

SB Energy, an AI infrastructure platform backed by SoftBank, registered for the initial public offering earlier this month. The company said it would trade on Nasdaq under the symbol SBE.

SB Energy is aiming to raise between $5 billion and $7 billion in the IPO, The Wall Street Journal has reported.

data.title: High Demand Turns Cart Wheels at Big Festive Bash
data.description:
Writankar Mukherjee & Sharmistha Mukherjee Kolkata|New Delhi: Consumer demand in India scaled a five-year high in the first phase of the festive season, lifting hopes of manufacturers across categories including home appliances, automobiles, apparel and footwear. Sales growth during the period spanning Onam, Rakshabandhan and Ganesh Chaturthi came despite several price increases, reflecting underlying consumer optimism.

Industry executives are hopeful the momentum will sustain till Navratri-Diwali, the country's largest consumption period. The latest demand upswing is broad-based across categories, according to executives. Online platforms, including quick commerce and food delivery services, also reported strong growth. Volume sales of refrigerators, air-conditioners and washing machines rose 12-15% year-on-year during the first phase, led by Onam, while value sales grew faster at 18-23% thanks to the price hikes, according to manufacturers.

Smaller towns in Maharashtra and Karnataka too reported robust sales growth since the weekend for Ganesh Chaturthi. "Onam gave us a very encouraging start, with good sell-out and healthy channel stocking. We are also seeing good growth around Ganesh Chaturthi, driven largely by volumes," said Sanjay Chitkara, director at LG Electronics, the country's largest white goods maker. Momentum is strong in large screen TVs, four-door refrigerators, large washing machines and ACs. Automakers, too, clocked record festive sales. Maruti Suzuki posted a 61% on-year rise in retail sales during Onam, despite the festival season being spread over fewer days this year.

data.title: Motherson to Invest 11,000cr in TN, Create 7,000 Jobs
data.description:
Our Bureau Chennai: Samvardhana Motherson, along with its European and UK-based joint venture companies, on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government to invest approximately Rs 11,000 crore in the state, creating around 7,000 employment opportunities.

The MoU was signed and exchanged in London by Barrie Painter, global head-marketing and communications, Samvardhana Motherson International Group, and Deepak Jacob, managing director, Guidance, Tamil Nadu government, in the presence of chief minister C Joseph Vijay.

The MoU is the first major investment announcement after Vijay arrived in the UK capital as part of his visit to attract investments and expand partnerships in sectors including advanced manufacturing, electric vehicles, electronics and global capability centres. The proposed investment will cover design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly and logistics facilities in Tamil Nadu and will span the next five years. "The investment brings Motherson's global joint venture network, technical partners from Europe and the UK, and its international capabilities to Tamil Nadu, further strengthening the state's position as a preferred destination for advanced manufacturing and global partnerships," Guidance said in a post on X.

The news of the proposed investment comes after the Opposition attacked the ruling TVK over the visit to London. The AIADMK on Monday questioned the need for such an overseas trip at taxpayers' expense. The party pointed out that a company established in India in 1986 and headquartered in Noida was among the businesses involved, raising questions over the rationale for Vijay travelling to the UK for investment promotion. "A company established in India in 1986, HQ Noida @actorvijay travels all the way to UK at taxpayers money to attract investment," AIADMK spokesperson Kovai Sathyan said in a post on X.

Earlier, the DMK, too, hit out at the chief minister claiming that the purpose of his visit was to "attend the car race of his friend Ajith". "He said that he is going to receive investment from London. But everybody saw that he had gone to see the car race of his friend Ajith," DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan said.

data.title: Coforge Appoints Egon Zehnder for Board Search
data.description:
Our Bureau Bengaluru: Coforge has appointed global executive search firm Egon Zehnder to identify a new chairman and two additional independent directors, following the board unrest with two exits last week of the mid-tier IT firm's chairman Om Prakash Bhatt and Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) chair DK Singh.

The existing board spoke to analysts on Monday, headed by interim chairman Vivek Sharma, who said he will oversee the process to elect a permanent chair but he would not be a candidate for the role. Sharma has been appointed as the interim chairman until January 31, 2027. On September 8, Bhatt resigned with immediate effect, following concerns around an internal audit over the company's board evaluation process under his watch.

data.title: Bessent Voices Support for Crypto Clarity Act Ahead of Key Vote — Market Talk
data.description: Treasury Secretary Bessent reiterated his support for the crypto Clarity Act ahead of a key Senate vote, calling the legislation "essential to ensuring America wins the global race for new technology." Bessent said on X that the act's final draft furthers the administration's mission of enabling digital technology while supporting community banks. That's been a point of contention, with critics worried that the legislation doesn't do enough to protect community banks from deposit flight caused by interest-like payments on stablecoin balances. Bessent said the draft gives the Treasury additional authority to safeguard community banks. "If stablecoins cause harm to community banks, I will not hesitate to use these tools to ensure they remain fully protected." The upcoming vote will decide if the act enters final voting procedures or gets pushed back. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

data.title: South Korea to develop new security guidelines for autonomous AI agents
data.description:
South Korea's state-run internet security agency said on Tuesday it is developing updated guidelines to manage the growing autonomy of AI systems, as companies deploy AI agents capable of operating with limited human oversight.

Here are the details:

  • The Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA), which operates under South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT, told Reuters it is working on an updated version of the "AI Security Guide", first published last year.

  • In a statement, KISA said the revised guide would focus on security issues that could arise as companies deploy agentic AI services and offer a checklist to manage those risks.

  • The agency also said the guide could include common control measures applicable to "physical AI" systems capable of interacting with real-world devices and machinery.

  • KISA said the new guide was designed to address risks posed by agentic AI systems more broadly and not specifically targeted at high-performance AI models, such as those implicated in the Hugging Face breach.

  • The July hack of the open-source repository Hugging Face, in which a swarm of roughly 700 AI agents created by OpenAI carried out a hack and in many cases tried to cover their tracks, has become a catalyst for a broader industry reckoning over how to govern increasingly autonomous AI systems.

data.title: ZAWYA: HORECA Oman opens fifth edition, uniting hospitality industry
data.description:
By Staff Writer

HORECA Oman opened its fifth edition at the Oman Convention & Exhibition Centre, bringing together hospitality and foodservice professionals from Oman and the wider region.

Co-organised by Hospitality Services and Al Nimr Expo, with support from the Ministry of Heritage and Tourism and the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources, the three-day exhibition runs until 16 September 2026.

The event features more than 200 exhibitors showcasing over 1,500 local and international brands across more than 5,500 square metres. Organisers expect more than 8,000 buyers and trade visitors to attend.

“HORECA Oman reflects the continued growth and dynamism of Oman’s hospitality sector,” said Joumana Dammous-Salamé, managing director of Hospitality Services. “It has become an important annual meeting place where professionals come together to discover what’s new, exchange ideas and expertise, meet the right partners and create new business opportunities. We are proud to see the event continue to grow alongside the industry it serves.”

Salim Al Hashmi, CEO of Al Nimr Expo, said: “HORECA Oman continues to support the advancement of the hospitality sector by bringing together professionals, innovators and emerging talents. This collaboration contributes to strengthening industry capabilities and positioning Oman as an evolving destination for hospitality investment and growth.”

The exhibition covers food and beverage, hotel and kitchen equipment, hospitality design and operations, alongside new technologies and solutions shaping the sector.

Industry knowledge and networking are also key elements of the programme.

HORECA Talks brings together industry leaders to discuss opportunities and challenges facing hospitality and foodservice in Oman and the wider region.

More than 30 competitions and masterclasses will feature over 250 competitors, including the Hospitality Salon Culinaire, Junior Chef Competition, Art of Service Competition, HORECA Barista Competition Oman and Latte Art Competition by the Specialty Coffee Association, as well as Mocktail and Bed Making competitions.

More than 40 speakers, experts and guest chefs will contribute through masterclasses, live cooking demonstrations and knowledge-sharing sessions.

Dedicated B2B meetings and networking opportunities will further support business development and partnerships.

Organisers said the event aims to strengthen connections across Oman’s hospitality and foodservice community while highlighting innovation, professional talent and investment opportunities in the sector.

data.title: Delta Electronics Thailand shareholder plans $1.5 billion bond issue
data.description:
Delta Electronics Thailand said on Tuesday that its major shareholder, Delta Electronics Int'l (Singapore), is seeking to raise $1.5 billion through bonds exchangeable into shares of the Thai company.

Here are the details:

  • The proposed bond issuance includes $500 million in bonds due in September 2027 and $1 billion in bonds due in September 2031, the company said.

  • The 2027 tranche carries an initial exchange price of 266.8 baht per share, representing a 15% premium to the reference price, while the 2031 tranche has an initial exchange price of 301.6 baht ($9.08) per share, a 30% premium.

  • The bonds will be exchangeable into existing Delta Electronics (Thailand) shares currently held by the Singapore-based shareholder, a unit of Taiwan-listed Delta Electronics Inc . The Singapore unit of Delta Electronics holds 42.85% of the company's shares, as per data compiled by LSEG.

  • If all exchange rights are exercised at the initial exchange prices, the bonds would be exchanged into about 172.1 million existing shares, equivalent to roughly 1.38% of Delta Electronics (Thailand)'s total issued shares.

  • The company added that the $1 billion 5-year bonds could be redeemed at 99.25% and 98.51% of the principal amount after 1.5 and 3 years, respectively, from the issuance date.

  • The proceeds from the bonds will strengthen working capital and support future business expansion.

($1 = 33.2300 baht)

data.title: ZAWYA: EXPRO adds flynas to government travel agreement
data.description:
By Staff Writer

The Government Expenditure and Projects Efficiency Authority (EXPRO) has announced the activation of flynas under the unified framework agreement for government travel services, in cooperation with the Ministry of Finance and the National Centre for Government Resource Systems.

The move increases the number of participating airlines to four, alongside Saudia, flyadeal and Riyadh Air, strengthening competition and expanding travel options for government employees and beneficiaries of government travel services.

The addition of flynas is expected to increase seat capacity, expand destination coverage and flight schedules, and provide greater booking flexibility and a wider range of service packages to meet the needs of public-sector travellers.

The activation will also expand travel options available through the Etimad platform, providing an integrated digital process covering travel order creation, flight booking and electronic ticket issuance.

EXPRO said the initiative will help improve operational efficiency while enhancing the customer experience.

The unified procurement framework is one of EXPRO’s contracting mechanisms for government entities under the Government Tenders and Procurement Law.

It enables the authority to negotiate unified agreements with service providers to achieve better value for public funds, reduce procurement time, standardize prices and service specifications, and improve service quality.

EXPRO said flynas’ activation forms part of its efforts to diversify suppliers and expand the number of participating carriers, supporting greater flexibility and efficiency in government travel services while meeting the evolving needs of government entities and beneficiaries.

data.title: Nifty stretched on the downside: Key reasons why a bounce back may be due
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 15 -- The Nifty ended another difficult week on a weak note, falling 499.60 points, or 2.09%, and extending its decline to five consecutive weeks.

The current run now equals the index's longest weekly losing streak of CY2026. The Nifty had earlier registered a similar five week decline between February and March.

Although the index recovered from lower levels in each of the last two sessions, the price structure remained weak. The rebounds were not strong enough to produce a higher low or take the index above the previous session's high.

Friday's recovery came after the Nifty tested the lower boundary of a declining channel. This has brought the session low of 23,231 into focus as an important near term support.

The overall structure, however, continues to favour the bears. The index has slipped below a cluster of Fibonacci support levels from the previous upswing and has also broken below the earlier swing low. With that, the trend setup has moved into a confirmed downtrend.

There are, however, signs that the recent fall may be overextended in the near term.

The Nifty has finished below the lower Bollinger Band for three consecutive sessions, a reading that often appears after a sharp directional move. If the index manages to defend Friday's low, some recovery or short covering could emerge over the next few sessions.

Momentum indicators are also reflecting the intensity of the recent selling. The daily 14 period RSI has moved into oversold territory, while the weekly RSI is now testing the 40 mark, an important zone from a medium term perspective.

These readings leave room for a technical bounce, but the larger trend will remain weak unless price starts reclaiming key resistance levels.

For the coming week, the immediate resistance area is placed between 23,572 and 23,623. This zone corresponds to the downside gap created on September 9 and is likely to act as the first major hurdle during any recovery.

A sustained move above this band would be an early sign of improvement in the short term structure. If the index manages to hold above the gap zone, the next resistance is seen near 23,940.

On the downside, 23,231 remains the key level to track. A decisive break below this support could resume the decline and strengthen the bearish setup further.

The oversold readings may allow the Nifty to attempt a rebound, but the September 9 gap remains the level that needs to be reclaimed before the near term picture improves meaningfully. With global markets still volatile, the broader setup continues to warrant caution below this resistance zone.

Stock to Watch: VA Tech Wabag (WABAG)

VA Tech Wabag has broken out of a 45 week cup pattern and closed at a fresh lifetime high. The breakout was supported by higher volumes, adding strength to the move. Its Relative Strength line has also reached a new high, indicating that the stock continues to outperform the broader market.

Both short term and long term moving averages are trending higher, while the moving average ribbon remains firmly in an uptrend. The Bollinger Bands are also rising and expanding across multiple time frames, reflecting improving Momentum and volatility.

Momentum indicators remain supportive. The MACD continues to stay bullish, while the weekly RSI has bounced after retesting the 60 zone. The daily 14 period RSI also remains in the strong bullish zone. In addition, the Stochastic RSI and KST continue to show positive momentum.

The Elder Impulse System has formed a strong bullish bar across multiple time frames, further supporting the positive technical setup.

The stock has also registered a 45 week cup pattern breakout. A sustained move above Rs.2,280 would keep the setup positive, with the stock potentially testing Rs.2,466. A stop loss can be maintained at Rs.2,160. Above Rs.2,466, the next level to watch is around Rs.2,610.

data.title: EQ Resources to take 10% stake in Nevada tungsten project JV with Elmet, Blue Moon
data.description:
Australian miner EQ Resources said on Tuesday it would take a 10% stake in a joint venture with Nasdaq-listed Elmet Group and Blue Moon Metals to restart the Springer tungsten project in Nevada.

Shares of EQ Resources jumped as much as 16.9% to A$0.45, their highest level in 19 years.

Here are more details:

  • Under the agreement, Elmet will hold a 70% stake and operate the project, while Canada-based Blue Moon and tungsten supplier EQ Resources will own 20% and 10%, respectively.

  • The joint venture plans to restart the Springer ammonium paratungstate (APT) plant in Nevada with an initial processing capacity of about 4,000 tonnes per year.

  • Elmet will fund the first $75 million of restart costs for the plant, backed by financing from the U.S. Department of Defense.

  • Elmet and EQ Resources will jointly fund costs between $75 million and $100 million based on their ownership stakes, with EQ's contribution capped at $3.125 million, while costs above $100 million will be shared by all partners pro rata.

  • EQ Resources will supply 4,000 tonnes of tungsten concentrate to the JV under an eight-year offtake arrangement, with the deal allowing it access for up to 1,000 tonnes per year of APT processing capacity at the plant during the first five years of operations.

  • "We are already producing tungsten from Australia and Spain, and this proposed joint venture gives us a pathway into downstream APT processing in the United States," said Craig Bradshaw, managing director of EQ Resources.

  • The company will also contribute its technical expertise, including engineering and project management oversight, and ore-sorting technology.

data.title: ANZ CEO says high taxes prevent Australia from being top Asian financial hub
data.description:
By Christine Chen

ANZ Group Chief Executive Nuno Matos said on Tuesday that Australia had some of the ingredients needed to become a regional financial hub, but its unfavourable tax regime was holding it back.

Matos said Australia had developing capital markets and a big pool of domestic savings through its compulsory pension system, two conditions that were important to becoming a financial centre.

But it lacked a tax regime that was attractive to foreign capital, unlike other financial centres in the Asia-Pacific region, he said.

"You also need to have very favourable taxation (to be a financial hub). And in that case, Australia does not have it," the Portuguese-born former HSBC executive told a conference in Sydney.

He said capital was not attracted to high-tax environments.

"Hong Kong and Singapore, they are basically 0% tax on capital," Matos said.

Australia should not "expect to be a financial hub if you don't attract capital, financial capital", he said, adding that "capital taxation needs to be different".

In June, Australia's parliament passed legislation scrapping the 50% capital gains tax discount on assets held for more than a year from July 1, 2027, returning to the pre-1999 policy of taxing inflation-indexed gains, with a 30% minimum tax on net capital gains.

Australia's parliament also passed legislation last week broadening the types of assets on which foreign residents are subject to capital gains tax.

Asked about the impact of AI on businesses, Matos said it was changing jobs and warned that workers who failed to adopt it would be left behind.

"If you are not an AI adopter, you will lose your job to someone that is an AI adopter," he said.

He did not rule out the possibility that AI could cause large-scale job losses at the bank, saying "nobody knows" what would happen. AI's development and adoption also needed to be accompanied by guardrails and limitations, he added.

"AI at this point in time is creating risks at a much higher pace than what their own builders and developers were thinking about it," he said.

The remarks come after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged AI companies to slow the rate at which they developed the technology.

The call was supported by Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI.

data.title: India's HDFC Bank rises as CEO succession process moves ahead
data.description:
Shares of India's HDFC Bank rose 2.94% on Tuesday, their biggest intraday percentage gain since May 6, after the country's largest private lender moved ahead with its CEO succession process, submitting names of two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India.

The bank said on Saturday it had submitted the two candidates without disclosing their names, as it looks to replace CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan, who is due to step down when his term ends on October 26.

The two candidates are HDFC Bank Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance CEO Anup Bagchi, NDTV Profit reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter. HDFC Bank did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

CEO succession has been a key investor concern for HDFC Bank since Sashidhar Jagdishan announced on August 29 that he would step down. In July, the bank's board penalised three top ​executives including Jagdishan after judging that employees involved in setting deposit rates for a state agency ​had engaged in "business overreach".

Analysts at Jefferies said the board had moved quickly, adding that an appointment before Jagdishan's term ends could ease investor concerns and limit the impact of leadership uncertainty on business momentum.

The brokerage said investors were comfortable with a leadership change, but felt the appointment should not include former leaders of state-owned banks as that could complicate the transition. Jefferies maintained its "buy" rating and 880-rupee price target.

HDFC Bank shares were up 2.28% at 724.10 rupees apiece as of 9:25 am IST.

data.title: Indian IT stocks jump after call for AI development slowdown
data.description:
Indian IT stocks jumped 5% after leaders of the world's biggest artificial intelligence companies warned of potentially existential risks from the technology.

IT stocks have been major laggards in the market over the last year as new AI tools threaten the business models of traditional software services companies.

data.title: Wiping out measles impossible due to vaccine hesitancy in rich countries, says Gates
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gates says measles eradication was once a potential goal for his charitable foundation
  • But vaccine hesitancy in rich countries has taken that off the table
  • On 2025 aid cuts, Gates says impact was tragic but most dire predictions did not play out

By Jennifer Rigby

Vaccine hesitancy in rich countries means ending measles as a global public health threat is not currently possible, Bill Gates told Reuters in an interview.

The Microsoft co-founder turned billionaire philanthropist said wiping out the killer childhood disease had previously been a potential goal for his eponymous foundation, which focuses on global health and the world’s poorest people.

But it was now off the table due to increased vaccine hesitancy in wealthier nations, part of a wave of skepticism championed for decades by the now health secretary in the United States under President Donald Trump, Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

“At one point, the foundation wanted to eradicate measles, but the vaccine hesitancy in rich countries has meant that’s not on our list of goals,” Gates said. “I think that’s kind of tragic.”

MEASLES RISE

Measles, among the world’s most contagious diseases, causes a high fever, a cough and a tell-tale rash.

The virus killed around 2 million children every year before the introduction of a vaccine in the 1960s. Nowadays, around 100,000 children die annually, largely in countries where conflict or logistics make immunisation difficult. The WHO says vaccination rates need to be above 95% to prevent outbreaks.

But recent years have also seen a surge in cases in countries where the disease was almost forgotten, including in the United States and Europe, as vaccination rates have fallen.

Gates said that vaccine hesitancy had at least not spread to lower-income countries, where measles can be much deadlier than in richer countries due to malnutrition and healthcare gaps.

“There’s always that concern that if you have doubters in the U.S., that becomes a global thing,” he said. “But we haven’t seen an increase in vaccine hesitancy in the countries the foundation works in.”

AID CUTS

Gates was speaking ahead of the foundation’s annual Goalkeepers event, which looks at progress towards the United Nations global development goals set for 2030, including on improving health.

In last year's report, Gates warned of the impact of aid cuts led by Trump’s administration, and followed by other wealthy countries like the UK and Germany, on the health of the world’s poorest.

This year, he said the cuts had likely caused many deaths, but the restoration of some money had prevented the worst-case scenario. Efforts from impacted countries and other health groups also held off disaster, as Reuters has reported.

“The most dire predictions, which went above 10 million deaths, we don’t see that taking place,” Gates said, adding that he continued to urge governments to restore aid or at least not cut it further. “It’s still a very tragic situation.”

data.title: Governments worldwide are way behind on AI, says Bill Gates
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gates says AI poses risk to jobs, risk of addiction and risk of attacks
  • But AI also has huge potential and Gates Foundation plans to spend $1 billion on equitable access
  • Governments must work together to solve the problem, Gates says

By Jennifer Rigby

No government in the world is ready for the changes artificial intelligence will bring to society, Bill Gates said in an interview with Reuters, as he warned of the risks ahead.

The Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist had until recently been optimistic about AI, but has changed his position, warning of the threats to jobs, concerns about attacks and the dangers of addiction to AI companions.

“I don't think any government is nearly as deep on this as they have to be,” he said. However, he added that the technology has great potential to help the world's poorest if managed properly and accessed equally — and his namesake foundation said on Tuesday that it plans to spend at least $1 billion in the next two years on expanding access to AI.

Gates said he has been talking to world leaders about his concerns, including President Donald Trump and his team in the U.S., and said he aims to meet China’s President Xi Jinping later this year.

“Governments are way behind on this one,” he added.

HEALTH POTENTIAL

But despite his concerns, Gates and his foundation hope AI can help narrow gaps between the richest and poorest, rather than widening them.

The foundation's $1 billion spending plan, part of its previously announced plans to spend $9 billion annually, will go to partners working in education, healthcare and agriculture, the foundation said. It also aims to help build the data foundations AI is built on, such as ensuring that large language models work in every language people speak.

“For health it’s hard to overstate what the potential is,” Gates said, from supporting frontline health care workers to discovering new drugs and vaccines.

But he said governments must work together to avoid problems, likening the arrival of AI to a disaster movie.

“There’s all sorts of movies where some aliens are coming, and magically the U.S. and China and everybody comes together to solve the problem,” he said. “AI is kind of like this alien intelligence. It’s here, and we better do like it shows in those movies.”

REPUTATIONAL HIT?

In June, Gates appeared in front of Congress to testify about his relationship with the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Gates, who is not accused of any crimes, has repeatedly said he regrets his association with Epstein, who he hoped would donate to global health causes. Instead, the financier attempted to blackmail Gates over his extramarital affairs.

However, despite prompting an external review at his foundation, which found no payments to Epstein or participation in criminal activities, Gates said the links had not caused him or the foundation a significant reputational hit.

“In terms of having access to government leaders, or you know, journalists being willing to interview me, I don't see any diminishment,” he said, adding that the desire to draw on the foundation’s expertise to cut child deaths and end malaria had also not reduced “even one iota”.
